run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-101 had issues on November 21, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The exact pod named in the question, a payment-api pod in namespace app-101, was not in the cluster when I queried it (2026-11-22T09:48:41Z): the only object in app-101 pods was loki-66445c6d6f-cz9mq. The namespace app-101 does exist, and Loki holds app-101 logs for a pod named payment-api-101-8486559b69-kkjmj (service=payment-api, job=payment-api, file /var/log/payment-api.log). Those logs are the evidence for the incident: between 13:46:00Z and 14:44:00Z on 2026-11-21 the pod logged 8 ERROR lines, all exactly "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted", with wait_time_ms 1227 to 4840 and queue_length 5 to 15. The first line of that error type is 13:46:00Z, 4 minutes after an INFO "Payment processed successfully" at 13:42:00Z, which matches the reported "around 13:45". In the 33 log lines returned across the full authorized window, there is no ERROR before 13:46 and successful payments continue during and after the error window (13:59, 14:49, 15:27, ...), so this looks like degradation, not a total outage. The immediate fault is therefore an exhausted database connection pool inside the payment-api application; why the pool exhausted (external database slowness/saturation, pool sizing, or a load surge) is not observable here: Prometheus and Jaeger were SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this Run, app-101 contains no database workload or service, and the payment-api pod/deployment was not present at query time, so there is no pod status, container termination reason, metric or trace evidence. Note also that Loki's app-101 log stream was produced by a short-lived log-shipping pod (python:3.9-slim plus grafana/promtail:2.9.0 sidecar) created 2026-11-22T09:46:48Z and stopped 09:47:02Z, with promtail configured for job=payment-api, namespace=app-101, path /var/log/*.log. The similarly named payment workload in namespace otel-demo (Deployment payment, service payment) is a different entity: it was 1/1 ready and is not shown as failing by anything I read.

claims.text: At 2026-11-22T09:48:41Z the pods query for namespace app-101 returned only one pod, loki-66445c6d6f-cz9mq (Running); no payment-api pod was present under that exact name in that namespace at that moment.
Loki contains app-101 log lines labelled namespace=app-101, pod=payment-api-101-8486559b69-kkjmj, service=payment-api, job=payment-api, filename=/var/log/payment-api.log.

Querying {namespace="app-101", level="ERROR"} for 2026-11-21T13:40:00Z-16:00:00Z returned 8 ERROR lines from pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-kkjmj, timestamps 13:46:00Z, 13:54:00Z, 14:03:00Z, 14:15:00Z, 14:19:00Z, 14:21:00Z, 14:31:00Z and 14:44:00Z; every one has message "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" with wait_time_ms between 1227 and 4840 and queue_length between 5 and 15.

The earliest connection-pool ERROR observed is 2026-11-21T13:46:00Z (wait_time_ms 1227, queue_length 10) and the preceding retained line is an INFO "Payment processed successfully" (payment_id PAY-5032) at 13:42:00Z.

The full-window query {namespace="app-101"} for 2026-11-21T09:49:00Z-2026-11-22T09:48:00Z returned 33 lines with none omitted; the first returned line is 2026-11-21T11:19:00Z, no ERROR appears in that set before 13:46:00Z, and INFO "Payment processed successfully" lines appear inside and after the error window (13:59:00Z, 14:49:00Z, 15:27:00Z, 17:01:00Z, ...).

Kubernetes events for app-101 show Deployment payment-api-101 scaling ReplicaSet payment-api-101-8486559b69 from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-22T09:46:48Z, which created pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-kkjmj with containers from images python:3.9-slim and grafana/promtail:2.9.0, and both containers were then stopped (reason Killing) at 2026-11-22T09:47:02Z.

The promtail-config ConfigMap in app-101 configures a scrape job named payment-api with labels job=payment-api and namespace=app-101 scraping /var/log/*.log, parsing timestamp, level, message, service and pod from JSON; this is how the app-101 payment-api lines reached Loki.

The distinctly named otel-demo payment workload (Deployment payment in namespace otel-demo, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) reports 1/1 ready and available replicas with conditions Available and NewReplicaSetAvailable; this is a different entity from the app-101 payment-api and its health does not describe app-101.

No database workload is visible in the cluster: the only StatefulSet returned was alertmanager in otel-demo, and the cluster-wide Service list (30 services) contains no database service, so the database that payment-api connects to is not observable through these Kubernetes objects.

Successful payments are logged inside the same error window and after it (INFO "Payment processed successfully" at 13:59:00Z, 14:49:00Z, 15:27:00Z, 17:01:00Z, ...), so the evidence shows partial/periodic failure to obtain database connections rather than a complete outage of payment processing.

The observed failure mode is database connection pool exhaustion in the payment-api application itself: attempts to acquire a DB connection waited 1.2-4.8 s and queued (queue_length up to 15) before failing, which points at the pool inside the payment-api process (sizing or connection turnover) as the proximate cause of the 13:46-14:44 errors.

An alternative remaining candidate is saturation or slowness of the external database that payment-api depends on (holding connections until the pool is drained); no object, metric or log for that database was observable in this Run, so this is unverified.

A third candidate is insufficient pool capacity relative to demand (max pool size or a traffic increase). No payment-api configuration (pool size, DB host) was readable: app-101 ConfigMaps hold only kube-root-ca.crt, loki-config and promtail-config, and the payment-api deployment was absent at query time, so this remains unverified.

Inspect the payment-api database pool settings (max pool size, acquire timeout, idle/validation) and the database server's own connection and latency metrics for 2026-11-21T13:40Z-15:00Z, since the pod's own logs stop at the acquire-failure level and do not say why connections were unavailable.

Add an alert on the "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" log pattern and on pool wait time/queue length for payment-api so the 13:46 onset is caught from the application side rather than from a user report.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for every query in this Run (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query and get_metric_names all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for target m0-otel-20260909), so no error-rate, latency, pool or kube-state-metrics series were available and no metric baseline exists for a trend comparison.

Jaeger was unreachable in this Run (traces_list_services, traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE); the Jaeger service list documented for the target does not include payment-api, so spans for this specific app may not exist even when Jaeger is up.

The payment-api pod and its deployment were not present in the cluster at query time (2026-11-22T09:48Z), so the incident-time pod status, container restart count, last termination reason and exit code are unknown; the pod name comes only from Loki labels and a log-replay pod created at 09:46:48Z on 2026-11-22.

Kubernetes events in the returned window are all from 2026-11-22T09:21-09:47Z (about the loki and log-replay pods), so there are no events covering 2026-11-21T13:45Z; what the scheduler/kubelet recorded then is unknown.

The database that payment-api failed to get connections from is not a Kubernetes object in this cluster (no DB StatefulSet/Deployment or Service), so its availability, connection count and latency around 13:45Z are unknown.

No payment-api configuration (DB host, pool size, acquire timeout) was readable; app-101 ConfigMaps contain only kube-root-ca.crt, loki-config and promtail-config, and pods/deployment for payment-api were absent.

A Loki line filter for timeout|slow|refused|oom|restart|panic|fatal|deadlock|max_connections|too many over 2026-11-21T11:00Z-15:00Z in app-101 returned no lines, so there is no corroborating log text about the DB side, restarts or OOM; that query result is a no_data view and is not cited as a fact.

Loki retention for the app-101 stream begins at 2026-11-21T11:19:00Z in the returned data, so any earlier degradation before that time is unknown, and the 33 returned lines appear to be a sampled/sparse subset of the pod's output.
The change_history integration is not available, so whether a deployment, pool-size change or database change preceded 13:46Z could not be checked.
